_comment: Tier-2 NUMERICAL GATE. EXERCISES THE NUMPY/SCIPY PATH, NOT KRATOS — the heat_transient catalog template declares 'Kratos (manual assembly)' and assembles K and M with scipy. Pitfall (kratos.heat_transient #1) states the Crank-Nicolson update as (M + 0.5*dt*K) T_new = (M - 0.5*dt*K) T_old. NOTE ON THE WRITTEN SIGNAL: this claim carries one of the five shared boilerplate Signal suffixes used across the Kratos catalog, which does not describe what actually happens. The real signal is recorded below and in the fixture output. The claim is a formula, so the fixture checks the property that makes the formula worth using: implemented exactly as written on the template's own K and M, it converges at order 2 in time, while the same code at theta=1 (backward Euler) converges at order 1, and Crank-Nicolson is the more accurate of the two at equal step size. The reference is the same scheme at 4096 steps, so no external solution is assumed. All numbers asserted are this fixture's own output; none is written into any knowledge text. This is also the correct scheme that the SHIPPED template fails to implement — see heat_transient_template_violates_maximum_principle for what the template does instead. Executed on Kratos 10.4.3 (pip wheels, glibc-2.31 host, fresh venv on external ext4 image). MUTATION CONTROL (added 2026-08-06, re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 runs the Crank-Nicolson leg with theta=1.0, i.e. backward Euler, so the scheme claimed to be second order is first order. cn_observed_order goes 2 -> 1.005, equal to the backward-Euler leg, and CN no longer beats BE at the same step. Verified: unmutated the fixture PASSES; with T2_MUTATE=1 it FAILS and these expect_in_output strings disappear: cn_order_near_2=True, cn_beats_be_at_same_dt=True, crank_nicolson_mismatches=0. Re-verify: cd scripts/tier2_fixtures/kratos/heat_transient_crank_nicolson_is_second_order && /usr/bin/python3 source.py (passes), then T2_MUTATE=1 /usr/bin/python3 source.py (fails). Interpreter: KRATOS_PYTHON=/usr/bin/python3 is REQUIRED on this host -- the repo venv Kratos wheel is built against GLIBC_2.32 and fails to load (ImportError on Kratos.cpython-312...so), while the system python3.8 carries Kratos 10.4 Release with CableNet, ConstitutiveLaws, StructuralMechanics and LinearSolvers.
